The consolidated Castrol EBITDA (~$0.9bn net of the retained 35% associate dividend) leaves the base from FY2027 via the -5% FY2027 revenue step and the flat dollar EBITDA that implies. historical_growth.growth_rate_source: through-cycle judgment: management guides underlying production broadly flat, refining footprint shrinking by design, so nominal growth is inflation on a flat real volume base. Every historical CAGR here is a commodity-price artefact (FY2020 pandemic trough base inflates the 5-yr revenue figure to +12%; FY2022 price-spike base makes the 3-yr figures -8% revenue / -29% owner FCF) and none is usable as a forward rate.
historical_growth.growth_divergence_warning: Equity CAGR (-5.7%/-7.7%) diverges from revenue by far more than 30% but the divergence is mechanical: equity shrank via $30bn of buybacks FY2021-25 plus $20bn+ of impairments (low-carbon write-downs, Gelsenkirchen, Turkiye), not via a loss of earning power. EPS CAGRs are null because the FY2020 and FY2022 bases are negative. The revenue basis also changed at the FY2020 restatement, so FY2018-19 revenue is not comparable with FY2020+ (owner FCF is unaffected).
historical_growth.notes: Owner-FCF (reported FCF less SBC) 3-yr CAGR of -29% against reported FCF -27%: SBC rose from $795m to $1,077m while FCF fell, so SBC is a growing (but still small, 0.57% of revenue) share of cash generation.

scenario_narratives.base: Mid-cycle integrated major: $70-75 Brent, flat underlying production, cost-out roughly offsetting divested EBITDA so dollar EBITDA holds ~$40bn, unlevered owner FCF ~$13.5-14bn from FY2027, net debt reaching the $14-18bn target in FY2026 via the Castrol proceeds and the buyback pause.
scenario_narratives.bull: Reset fully delivered at $75-80 Brent: $6.5bn cost-out, 2027 targets (>16% ROACE, ~$15bn adjusted FCF) met, reserve replacement sustains volumes, buybacks resume, governance discount closes toward Shell's multiple.
scenario_narratives.bear: Sustained $60-65 Brent oversupply with refining margins normalising; EBITDA ~$34bn, capex floor binds, deleveraging stalls above $18bn, buybacks stay suspended and governance turmoil continues. Still cash-generative; no solvency path modelled.

valuation_philosophy.summary: A through-cycle owner-FCF DCF anchored on FY2025, which BP itself says was a ~$70-real price environment, rather than on the H1-2026 Middle-East price spike. EBITDA is built from the cash flow statement (after decommissioning spend, before Gulf of America payments), leases are charged as an operating cost at the full $3.8bn cash cost with lease liabilities kept out of net debt, and every claim ranking ahead of ordinary shareholders - $22.3bn net debt, $15.5bn of hybrids, $4.9bn other NCI and the $5bn net GoA liability - is deducted once in the bridge, with the signed $5.5bn net Castrol proceeds credited. Risk is charged once: one 8% USD WACC across scenarios, with cyclicality and governance carried in the driver paths and a 25/50/25 weighting. The terminal value is capped at 12x owner FCF (10x bear, 13x bull), well inside the market's historical treatment of BP, so the base case assumes no re-rating. The investment framing is income plus modest nominal growth with a deleveraging-driven re-rating option, not a multi-bagger.
key_risks_to_valuation: Commodity price path: BP's own rules of thumb are ~$340m pre-tax per $1/bbl Brent and $450m per $1/bbl RIM for a full year; a sustained $10 miss on Brent is ~$2bn of after-tax FCF, or roughly 15% of the base-case flow.
Disposal execution: Castrol ($6bn), UK North Sea (~GBP2bn) and the rest of the $20bn programme must close on terms for net debt to reach $14-18bn; the bridge credits Castrol only.
Cost-out delivery versus inflation: the base assumes cost cuts merely offset divested EBITDA; if they fall short, the 21.5% margin is the first driver to give.

Claims ahead of equity: hybrids, GoA and other NCI total ~$25bn (~$1.60/share, ~120p) and are deducted at face/book; a buyer who treats hybrids as permanent equity would see ~17% more value than this model.
Governance: a fourth CEO since 2020 and a chair removed after seven months; another leadership break would push weights toward bear.

Half-year overlap and FX: FY2026 modelled as a full year against a 30-Jun-2026 balance sheet (~2% upward bias), and every per-share output moves 1:1 with GBPUSD, which refresh_price.py does not update.

sanity_check_note.why_this_note_exists: scripts/sanity_check.py applies inputs.fx_rate backwards for every currency != quote_currency ticker (see memory: sanity-check-fx-rate-direction-systemic-bug, -conflict; seventh occurrence AAF.L is the same USD-filer/GBp-quote shape). Its historical_table multiplies the pence price by 75.57 instead of dividing, so the printed history (P/B avg 8,112x, EV/EBITDA avg 18,934x) is off by fx_rate^2 = 5,711x and the printed implied multiples (P/B 204x, EV/EBITDA 369x) by fx_rate once. The script's 'passed: true' is therefore built on nonsense and has been forced to false in the sanity_check block so the eval gate shows red rather than a meaningless pass. No driver was changed because of the script output.
sanity_check_note.hand_bridged_basis: FY-end LSE close in GBp (script price / 75.57) converted to USD at the same static GBPUSD 1.3233 the script uses, direction corrected; market cap on the CSV diluted weighted-average share count; EV = market cap + (TotalDebt - Cash) from the CSV (finance debt only, leases excluded, consistent with lease treatment B); EBITDA is the CSV statutory figure (after impairments) and its SBC-adjusted twin. Implied multiples use the model's 15,409m share count, FY2025 denominators, and for the 'all claims' EV the model's own bridge (net debt + hybrids + other NCI + GoA - Castrol proceeds).

historical_range_hand_bridged.years: FY2019-FY2025 (FY2018 lacks equity/debt; FY2020 EBITDA negative)

sanity_check_note.determination: On the corrected basis the P/B rule (2.61x vs 1.77x 10-yr max) and the P/Sales rule (0.73x vs 0.64x max) WOULD trip; EV/EBITDA (5.45x SBC-adjusted vs 6.00x max, 4.15x average) passes, and the price_position_in_10yr_range of 108% shows the CURRENT price is already above its range on P/B (2.25x). The two excursions are denominator effects, not peak-earnings extrapolation: bp shareholders' equity fell from $98bn (FY2019) to $53bn (FY2025) through ~$35bn of buybacks and $20bn+ of impairments, and revenue is shrinking by design (Gelsenkirchen, Castrol, retail exits) while EBITDA holds, so P/B and P/S rise mechanically for an unchanged enterprise value. For an asset-heavy cyclical the rules that carry information are EV/EBITDA and FCF yield, and both sit inside the historical range at the IV.
step_8c5_fixes_already_embedded: Item 1 (mid-cycle FCF): FY0 = FY2025 at $69 Brent, which BP states was ~$13bn adjusted FCF on BOTH reported and $70-real price-adjusted bases; the H1-2026 $104-Brent run-rate is not annualised (see inputs.mid_cycle_fcf).
Item 3 (growth cap): nominal growth 1.5% from FY2028, below any through-cycle revenue CAGR.

Item 4 (exit-multiple cap at historical EV/EBITDA): base terminal cap of 12x owner FCF = $183bn on terminal-year EBITDA of $44.9bn = 4.1x, equal to the hand-bridged 10-yr SBC-adjusted AVERAGE of 4.15x; bear 10x FCF = 3.4x (hist min 3.0x); bull 13x FCF = 4.4x (hist max 6.0x). The cap binds in all three scenarios.
Item 2 (WACC premium): deliberately not applied - risk is charged once, in the flows and the 25/50/25 weights (owner-fcf-adaptations (f)).
sanity_check_note.fix_applied: No driver change. The prescribed mid-cycle anchor and historical-average EV/EBITDA exit cap were built in from the start, so applying them again would change nothing; the residual P/B and P/S excursions are denominator artefacts of a buyback-shrunk book and a deliberately shrinking revenue base, and the current price already sits above the P/B range. The valuation's re-rating content is stated explicitly: the base IV requires BP to hold ~5.5x SBC-adjusted EV/EBITDA (vs 4.8x today and a 4.15x 10-yr average, 6.0x max) - a modest deleveraging-driven re-rate, not peak-multiple extrapolation.

inputs.sbc_source: FY2025 Annual Report & 20-F, group cash flow statement 'Share-based payments' add-back (BP.L_Annual_FY2025.txt:11685), $ million. BP publishes no separate net-share-settlement tax line; equity awards are largely satisfied from treasury shares, so the add-back is used as the combined figure.
inputs.buyback_note: FY2025 'Repurchase of shares' $4,486m (cash flow statement :11705). Buyback programme SUSPENDED Feb 2026 with excess cash directed to the balance sheet; the flat count is therefore a modelling convention from FY2026 onward, not a funded one, until buybacks resume.
inputs.fx_note: Model currency USD -> quote currency GBp (pence). GBPUSD=X 1.3233 (Yahoo Finance, 2026-10-09T21:29Z), so 1 USD = 100/1.3233 = 75.57 GBp. Parity check against the NYSE ADR (1 ADS = 6 ordinary shares): 586.3p x 6 / 100 x 1.3233 = $46.55 vs BP ADR regular close $46.25 on 2026-10-09, a 0.6% tie confirming rate, direction and pence basis. refresh_price.py moves the price but not this rate; re-derive the rate on any later refresh.
inputs.balance_sheet_note: net_debt $22.3bn is BP's own definition (finance debt less cash, with fair-value hedge adjustments) at 30 June 2026 from the 2Q 2026 results presentation (BP.L_Presentation_Q2-2026.txt:315); it was $22.2bn at 31-Dec-2025 so the two vintages agree. total_debt/cash are the 31-Dec-2025 balance-sheet components (finance debt 3,356 + 54,602; cash 36,556; :11627/:11637/:11648) because the interim does not print them separately. Hybrids, hybrid securities, GoA liability are 30-Jun-2026 figures (:315-:323); other NCI is 31-Dec-2025 book (:11657 less hybrids). Half-year overlap: FY2026 is modelled as a full year-1 flow against a mid-2026 balance sheet; the ~$2.7bn of H1-2026 dividends already paid out of that flow is a ~2% upward bias, offset by the engine discounting FY2026 a full period from an October-2026 valuation date.
inputs.share_count_basis: 15,377.2m ordinary shares outstanding at 31-Dec-2025 excluding treasury and INCLUDING shares issuable under employee share plans (FY2025 AR Note 11, :13741), less the 48.5m net reduction to 13-Feb-2026 (:13742-13743), plus the 80.6m dilutive effect of share options (:13755) = 15,409m fully diluted. Held FLAT: SBC is fully expensed in the flows (charging both would double-count), and the buyback was suspended in Feb 2026 so no further shrinkage is assumed. ADS equivalent (1 ADS = 6 ordinary) = 2,568m.
inputs.wacc_rationale: USD WACC, built in the currency of the flows: 10-year UST ~4.2% + 5.0% ERP x beta ~0.95 = ~9.0% cost of equity; after-tax cost of debt ~3.5% on finance debt + hybrids + leases (~30% of capital) -> ~7.4% blended. House uses 8.0% in all three scenarios as a USD integrated-major rate. No cyclicality or governance premium is stacked on WACC: those risks are charged ONCE, in the mid-cycle flows and the 25/50/25 scenario weights (adaptations (f)).
inputs.lease_treatment: Treatment (B), leases as operating cost: full FY2025 lease cash cost of $3,763m (lease liability principal payments $3,091m in financing :11706 + lease interest $672m inside interest paid, :26013) is charged inside EBIT via lease_cost_pct_path (~2.0% of revenue); lease liabilities ($13.3bn net at 30-Jun-2026, $14.6bn gross at 31-Dec-2025) are EXCLUDED from net debt; D&A for the tax shield is ex right-of-use depreciation (17,822 - 3,028 ROU = 14,794, Note 12 :13847). This matches BP's own adjusted-FCF definition (OCF less capex less lease liability payments).
inputs.nci_treatment: Flows are consolidated (100%), so every non-shareholder claim is deducted once in the equity bridge: perpetual hybrid bonds $13.0bn and perpetual hybrid securities $2.5bn (both classified within NCI; coupons of ~$1.2bn/yr are paid in financing activities and so are OUTSIDE the EBITDA-based flows), and other NCI at book $4.95bn (total NCI 20,948 at 31-Dec-2025 less 13,500 hybrid bonds less 2,500 securities). Not deducted twice: the NCI share of profit is not removed from the flows.

mid_cycle_fcf.framing: Through-cycle anchor built in from the start, not as a post-hoc fix. FY0 = FY2025, in which Dated Brent averaged $69.10/bbl against BP's own $70/bbl (2024 real) price-adjusted reference, Henry Hub ~$3.5 vs $4 reference and RIM modestly above the $10.3 reference; BP states FY2025 adjusted FCF was ~$13bn on BOTH a reported and a price-adjusted basis (FY2025 results script :505). H1 2026 (Brent $104 in 2Q, RIM $29.6, adjusted FCF $14.4bn in six months) is a Middle-East-disruption peak and is deliberately NOT annualised; FY2026 gets a +3% revenue / +0.7pp margin nudge only.
mid_cycle_fcf.basis_note: History above is reported FCF (OCF - capex) less SBC: levered (after ~$2.3bn net interest), after Gulf of America payments (~$1.2bn) and after a $4.8bn FY2025 working-capital build. The component build is unlevered and ex-WC with GoA moved to the bridge, so its FY0 equivalent is ~$12.5bn: 10,195 + 2,315 net interest - ~900 interest tax shield + 1,200 GoA + 4,820 WC build - ~5,100 of tax/capex timing noise reconciles to BP's ~$13bn adjusted FCF less $1.1bn SBC.

inputs.notes: MODEL: owner-FCF component DCF (SKILL.md routing row 'operating company, non-US or cyclical'), with the adaptations file applied: dual currency (USD flows, GBp quote), lease treatment (B), NCI/hybrids charged once in the bridge, risk charged once (flat WACC, scenarios carry cyclicality). BP is an integrated oil & gas operating company, not a bank/REIT/LIC, so the FCF engine is the right tool; the sector adaptation is the through-cycle anchor described in mid_cycle_fcf. Cash EBITDA of ~$39.4bn (20.8% of revenue) is derived from the FY2025 cash flow statement: profit before tax 7,746 + exploration write-off 343 + DD&A 17,822 + impairments 5,050 - JV/associate earnings 618 + JV/associate dividends 2,111 + finance costs 5,106 - interest receivable 1,352 - pension finance 210 + SBC 1,077 - pension contributions 152 + net provision charge less payments 1,294 + GoA payments ~1,200 (moved to the bridge). It is therefore AFTER decommissioning cash spend and BEFORE SBC, leases, tax, interest and working capital. interest_income is 0 in the owner-FCF deduction because BP carries net debt, not net cash; the $1,352m interest receivable is nonetheless stripped from EBITDA above and the matching $36.6bn cash sits inside net debt (matching-asset rule). FreeCashFlow in the CSV does not deduct lease principal; the model does, inside EBIT. EPS in the CSV is in dollars per ordinary share. Rosneft 19.75% stake carried at nil; no bridge credit. Pension surplus ($7.8bn) not credited.
inputs.gaps: No 30-Jun-2026 finance-debt/cash split, share count or ROU depreciation in the interim presentation; FY2025 figures used for those components with the Q2-2026 net debt total overriding. BP does not disclose equity-award tax withholding separately.

bear.narrative: Oversupply persists: OPEC+ unwinds and non-OPEC growth hold Brent at $60-65 and RIM back near $10, so EBITDA falls to ~$34bn despite cost cuts; the North Sea and other disposals clear at distressed prices on a shrinking revenue base; capex cannot fall below ~$13.5bn without accelerating decline (so capex intensity rises to 7.8% of a smaller base and D&A to 8%); deleveraging stalls above $18bn, the buyback suspension becomes semi-permanent and the dividend is held flat in nominal terms; a third chair in two years and continued Elliott pressure keep the governance discount in place. No zero-floor hit: BP remains cash-generative even here.

base.growth_rationale: FY2026 +3%: H1 price tailwind (Brent ~$95 average) partly offset by lower volumes (production guided 2.18-2.27 vs 2.31 mmboe/d, refinery throughput down on Gelsenkirchen) and the Castrol/Turkiye/Austria/Netherlands exits. FY2027 -5%: prices assumed back at ~$72-75 nominal Brent, Castrol 65% and the UK North Sea upstream (~117 kboe/d) deconsolidated. Then +1.5% nominal = inflation on flat real volumes.
base.margin_rationale: 21.5% vs 20.8% FY2025 cash-EBITDA margin: $2bn of the $5.5-6.5bn structural cost target was delivered in 2025 with a further ~$3bn to come by end-2027, roughly offsetting divested EBITDA (~$1.5-2bn: Castrol, Gelsenkirchen, North Sea) and inflation. In dollars this is ~$39.8bn FY2027 EBITDA on a $185bn base, i.e. flat on FY2025 - management's plan is for materially more, so base assumes partial delivery.
base.capex_rationale: FY2026 guidance $13.5-14.0bn = 7.0% of modelled revenue; $13-15bn frame thereafter = 7.3%. D&A ex-ROU guided ~flat at ~$14.5bn = 7.5-7.6%; capex ~= D&A is consistent with flat volumes.
base.tax_rationale: Cash tax 38%: FY2025 cash tax paid $6.6bn plus ~$0.9bn interest shield on modelled EBIT of $19.8bn; FY2026 underlying ETR guided 35-40% (1H26 ran at 33%). Upstream fiscal regimes (UK EPL, Norway, Angola, Azerbaijan) keep BP's rate structurally above the 25% UK headline.
base.terminal_rationale: Gordon at 1.0% nominal (flat-to-declining long-run oil volumes partly offset by inflation) with the terminal value capped at 12x owner FCF - the low end of the 12-15x cyclical range, since BP has traded at ~5-6x EV/EBITDA and ~8-12x FCF for a decade.
base.narrative: Mid-cycle BP: $70-75 Brent, RIM ~$12-15, flat underlying production, the structural cost programme roughly paying for divested EBITDA, net debt into the $14-18bn range during FY2026 on Castrol proceeds and the buyback suspension, dividends maintained, buybacks resuming only once gearing is inside target. Value is the through-cycle ~$13-14bn of unlevered owner FCF, not the H1-2026 $104 Brent run-rate.

bull.narrative: The reset delivers: full $6.5bn structural cost-out with opex driven toward Elliott's sub-$13bn, Brent averaging ~$75-80 through the decade, the 2027 >16% ROACE and >20% price-adjusted adjusted-FCF CAGR targets met (unlevered owner FCF ~$16-17bn by FY2027), exploration (Bumerangue, GTA, Tiber-Guadalupe) sustaining a 90%+ reserve-replacement ratio so real volumes hold through 2035, net debt below $14bn allowing buybacks to resume at $4-5bn/yr, and O'Neill plus a settled chair closing the governance discount to Shell. Terminal cap lifted to 13x on a re-rated balance sheet.

required_return_table.note: Each row rebuilds the terminal value at that row's rate (max(0, min(Gordon@r, 12x FCF_N))); the WACC row is valuation.base.intrinsic_value and the hurdle row is entry_price.base.entry_price.

sensitivity.note: Rows are WACC, columns terminal growth; each cell rebuilds its own terminal value.

probability_weighted.weights_rationale: Moved from the house 15/50/35 to 25/50/25. Bull cut to 25% because it needs several independent things to go right - full cost delivery, mid-cycle-plus prices, disposals closing at value, and a settled board under a CEO six months into the job - after a reversed strategy and two chair changes. Bear raised to 25% because a sustained sub-$65 Brent oversupply (the IEA 2025 imbalance was ~2.2 mmb/d) is a live macro outcome rather than a tail, and BP's balance sheet is the weakest among the Western majors so it amplifies that downside; no going-concern or covenant risk, which is why bear is not 35%.

sanity_check.basis: SBC-adjusted on both sides (EPS less SBC/share; EBITDA less SBC), so these deliberately do not match GAAP screener multiples.
